correctness.rationale: The facet list reconstructs an (8,24,17) complex. The exhaustive recursion ranges over every injective triangle-to-boundary-edge matching with one critical triangle and rejects exactly those creating a closed V-path by maintaining directed transitive closure. It finds 1,992,223 accepted layers and zero acyclic layers matching all 17 triangles. Every accepted residual eight-edge graph is verified connected and hence unicyclic; its cycle histogram sums to the accepted count. The rooted-spanning-tree bijection gives exactly 8ℓ compatible vertex-edge layers for residual cycle length ℓ, yielding 63,617,968 full fields. Euler's relation and the zero count for a critical-triangle-free layer prove that three critical cells are minimal. Risk: correctness of the finite result depends on the verifier implementation, mitigated by explicit completeness arguments, internal invariants, exact integer arithmetic, and agreement with the published optimum vector.

value.rationale: The dunce hat is a canonical contractible noncollapsible obstruction and a standard benchmark in discrete Morse algorithms. A complete census of optimal gradient fields on its minimal eight-vertex model is a natural state-space invariant rather than an arbitrary parameter slice. The residual-unicycle factorization explains the 63,617,968 count structurally and supplies a six-cell distribution useful for benchmarking randomized or heuristic gradient constructions. The result is confined to one labelled combinatorial type, but that limitation does not remove the benchmark value.
